extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars of folklore, and creative writers studying folktale structure
extracted.subtask_description: Analyze or construct folktales using Vladimir Propp's morphology: identify the presence/ordering of 31 narrative functions and assignment of 7 character spheres to evaluate folktale-style structure and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absentation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of Propp's 31 functions (fixed order). Often initiates events by creating absence that motivates action. When absentation is missing or altered, folktale-type feel may weaken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdiction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function requiring a warning or prohibition directed at the hero; part of the fixed sequence. Failure to include this can change the moral/causal dynamics of the tale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow-up function where interdiction is violated; preserves causal chain leading to misfortune. Skipping can obscure motivation for subsequent misfortune.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconnaissance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Villain's active search for a victim or advantage; one of the ordered functions. Omitting reconnaissance can make villainy less agentive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The villain obtains information about the victim/situation; part of sequence that enables trickery or attack.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trickery
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An attempt by the villain to deceive the victim; contributes to the narrative conflict and leads to complicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Victim is taken in by deception
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Victim's gullibility or being misled is formalized as a function; helps justify ensuing harm or loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Villainy / Lacking
rubrics_metrics.description: Harm is done OR something is lacking
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central problem of the tale: an act of villainy or an absence/need. This function typically motivates the hero's quest or response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mediation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announcement of the misfortune and the call to action for a hero; transitions from problem to response phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beginning Counteraction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hero's decision to address the misfortune; marks the start of the quest/response sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical or symbolic departure initiating the quest; part of the fixed order of functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Donor Function
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Donor tests or prepares the hero; sets up acquisition of magical aid or assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hero's Reaction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hero's reaction determines whether they receive the donor's gift; moral/behavioral test important for subsequent success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt of Magical Agent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquisition of an object/ability that enables progress; commonly follows a successful donor interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Hero is led to object of search
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assistance in locating the goal or next plot point; maintains narrative momentum toward the struggle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Struggle
rubrics_metrics.description: Hero and villain in direct combat
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct confrontation between hero and antagonist; typically a climactic function in the fixed sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A distinguishing mark or scar that functions later in recognition or verification; part of the ordered functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Victory
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolution of the antagonist; formal victory function that precedes liquidation of misfortune.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquidation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The problem introduced earlier is remedied; often follows victory and restores order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hero's return journey after accomplishing the task; part of the sequence leading to recognition and reward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursuit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A function where the hero faces pursuit during return; may create tension requiring rescue or aid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescue
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intervention that saves the hero from pursuit; often provided by helpers or magical means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unrecognized Arrival
rubrics_metrics.description: Hero arrives home or elsewhere unrecognized
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hero's anonymous return that sets up recognition, trials, or false claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfounded Claims
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduction of a false claimant who takes credit or makes false assertions, creating further conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficult Task
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A trial or task set to test the hero and provide opportunity for demonstration of worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful completion of the difficult task; often a step toward recognition and reward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revealing the hero's true identity or deeds; typically precedes reward and punishment of wrongdoers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The unmasking of imposture or wrongdoing; restores moral clarity before final transfiguration or punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfiguration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restorative or elevating change to the hero's form/standing prior to reward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punishment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final sanction applied to wrongdoers; completes moral resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wedding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal reward and social reintegration; often the tale's denouement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Villain (Character Sphere)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of Propp's 7 character spheres; note that functions are independent of who performs them — a character may fulfill multiple spheres or functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donor (Character Sphere)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepares hero or gives a magical object
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provider of tests and magical aids; occupies the donor sphere regardless of specific identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Helper (Character Sphere)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures who enable the hero's success through aid or guidance; may overlap with donor roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Princess / Her Father (Character Sphere)
rubrics_metrics.description: The prize / one who assigns difficult tasks
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Object of the quest or authority figure who delegates tasks; often motivates actions and rewards the hero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispatcher (Character Sphere)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sends the hero on the quest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agent who initiates the hero's mission by calling them to action; distinct from donor/ helper roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hero (Character Sphere)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protagonist who reacts to donor and weds the princess
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central character whose functions and actions drive the narrative; may occupy multiple functional positions in sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: False Hero (Character Sphere)
rubrics_metrics.description: Takes credit for hero's actions, claims princess
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An impostor or usurper who complicates recognition and reward; often exposed in later functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions are stable, constant elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions are stable, constant elements independent of who fulfills them
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytic principle: evaluate tales by mapping events to functions irrespective of which character performs them; encourages focusing on structure rather than surface detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited number of functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of functions is limited (31)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propp's claim that tale structure is composed from a closed set of functions; use this as a checklist when analyzing completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed sequence of functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The sequence of functions is identical across tales
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propp asserts an invariant order — sequence integrity is a key evaluative dimension; reordering is marked and may weaken folktale-typicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single structural type
rubrics_metrics.description: All fairy tales are of one structural type
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad theoretical claim: use Propp's morphology to compare tales within a unified structural framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness (evaluative dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative can be analyzed for completeness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for presence or absence of Propp's functions; missing core functions indicate an incomplete folktale structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence integrity (evaluative dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative can be analyzed for sequence integrity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether functions appear in the fixed order Propp describes; skipping or reordering core functions tends to weaken folktale-style structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character-function alignment (evaluative dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative can be analyzed for character-function alignment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how characters occupy Propp's spheres and whether functions are appropriately assigned; mismatches may alter how 'folktale-like' the story reads.
